examples.en: Our baby's skin is really smooth.
After grinding the stone for a long time, its surface became smooth.
Do your hands get smooth if you put on this lotion?
The floor is so smooth that it's slippery to walk on.

examples.ko: 삶은 달걀 껍질을 벗기니 매끈매끈한 속살이 나왔어요.
examples.en: When I peeled the boiled egg, a smooth white came out.

examples.ko: 새로 산 냄비는 안쪽이 매끈매끈하고 가벼워요.
examples.en: The new pot is smooth on the inside and light.

explain: '매끈하다'를 반복해서 더 부드럽고 고르게 느껴지는 말이에요. 만졌을 때의 느낌과 눈으로 보이는 모습에 모두 써요. '반들반들'은 윤이 나는 느낌이 강하고, '매끈매끈'은 거칠거나 울퉁불퉁한 곳이 없는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It repeats '매끈하다' to stress a smooth, even feel. You can use it both for how something feels to the touch and how it looks. '반들반들' stresses shine, while '매끈매끈' stresses having no rough or bumpy spots.

examples.en: I make sure to eat rice at every meal.
It's hard to make new side dishes for every meal.
Lately I've been eating only salad at every meal.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 매끼 밥을 두 공기씩 먹어요.
examples.en: My child eats two bowls of rice at every meal.

examples.ko: 이 약은 매끼 식사 후에 드세요.
examples.en: Take this medicine after every meal.
If there's no kimchi at every meal, it feels empty to me.

explain: '끼니마다'와 같은 뜻이에요. '매일', '매주'처럼 '매-'가 붙어서 '하나하나마다'라는 뜻을 더해요. 끼니를 셀 때는 '한 끼, 두 끼'라고 하고, 하루 세 끼를 모두 말할 때는 '삼시 세끼'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '끼니마다'. Like 매일 and 매주, the prefix '매-' adds the sense of 'each and every'. Meals are counted with '끼', as in 한 끼, 두 끼. For all three meals of the day, people also say '삼시 세끼'.

examples.ko: 이번 주 안에 이 일을 꼭 매듭지을게요.
examples.en: I'll definitely wrap up this matter within this week.
We couldn't settle that issue at the meeting.

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 이야기를 여기서 매듭짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to wrap up this topic here today.

examples.ko: 그 일을 잘 매듭지은 다음에 쉬세요.
examples.en: Rest after you've wrapped that work up properly.

examples.ko: 둘 사이의 오랜 싸움을 어떻게 매듭지을까요?
examples.en: How should we put an end to the long fight between the two of them?

examples.ko: 계약 문제는 이번 달에 매듭지을 거예요.
examples.en: We'll settle the contract issue this month.

explain: 실제로 끈을 묶는 것보다 일이나 문제, 이야기를 정리해서 끝낸다는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. '끝내다'보다 얽혀 있던 것을 마무리한다는 느낌이 있고, '마무리 짓다'와 비슷해요. 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라서 '매듭지어요, 매듭지으니까'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It is used far more often for wrapping up a task, problem or story than for tying a real knot. Compared with '끝내다', it suggests settling something that was tangled, and it is close to '마무리 짓다'. It is a ㅅ-irregular verb: 매듭지어요, 매듭지으니까.

examples.en: I rode in the car for a long time and now I feel sick.
My stomach gets queasy when I eat greasy food.

examples.ko: 어제부터 계속 매스꺼운데 병원에 가야 할까요?
examples.en: I've felt nauseous since yesterday. Should I go to the hospital?
As soon as I got on the boat, I started to feel sick.
The smell was so strong that it made me nauseous.
I felt a little nauseous after taking the medicine.

explain: '메스껍다'와 같은 뜻으로, 토할 것 같은 속의 느낌을 말해요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '매스꺼워요, 매스꺼운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람의 행동이나 말이 역겹다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It means the same as '메스껍다', the feeling of being about to throw up. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: 매스꺼워요, 매스꺼운. It can also be used figuratively for someone's behavior or words that disgust you.

examples.ko: 저는 요즘 일에 매여서 여행도 못 가요.
examples.en: I'm tied up with work these days, so I can't even travel.
The cow is tied to a post.
The shoelaces are tied tightly.

examples.ko: 저는 돈에 매여 살고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to live tied down by money.

examples.ko: 시간에 매이지 않고 자유롭게 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work freely, not bound by time.
I'm tied down by the kids, so I have no time.

explain: '매다'의 피동으로, 끈 같은 것에 묶여 있다는 뜻과 일이나 사람, 시간에 얽혀서 자유롭지 못하다는 비유로 써요. 비유로는 '얽매이다'와 비슷하고, 일상에서는 '묶이다'도 많이 말해요. 보통 '~에 매이다' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '매다'. It means being tied by a rope, and figuratively being stuck with a job, person or schedule and not free. In the figurative sense it is close to '얽매이다', and in daily talk people also say '묶이다'. It is usually used as '~에 매이다'.

examples.en: That actor's voice is truly captivating.
A captivating scent spread through the room.
Jeju Island is a fascinating place in all four seasons.
That offer is tempting, but it's difficult right now.

examples.ko: 노을 지는 바다가 아주 매혹적으로 보였어요.
examples.en: The sea at sunset looked very enchanting.
That singer sings with a captivating gaze.

explain: '매력적'과 비슷하지만 마음을 확 끌어당기는 더 강한 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '매력 있다'를 더 많이 말하고, 글이나 방송에서 '매혹적인 목소리'처럼 자주 나와요. 뒤에 '-인', '-이다', '-으로'를 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '매력적' but stronger, suggesting something that pulls you in. In daily talk people say '매력 있다' more often, while '매혹적' shows up in writing and broadcasts, as in '매혹적인 목소리'. It is used with '-인', '-이다' or '-으로'.

examples.en: Today the stars are clearly visible even to the naked eye.

examples.ko: 이 벌레는 너무 작아서 맨눈으로 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This bug is so small that it's hard to see with the naked eye.

examples.ko: 맨눈으로 일식을 보면 눈이 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: Watching an eclipse with the naked eye can hurt your eyes.

examples.ko: 안경을 벗으면 맨눈 시력이 아주 나빠요.
examples.en: Without my glasses, my uncorrected eyesight is very bad.
There's also a lot of dust that's hard to confirm with the naked eye.
The colors look different even with the naked eye.

explain: 안경, 망원경, 현미경 같은 도구 없이 눈만으로 본다는 뜻이에요. 대부분 '맨눈으로'의 형태로 나와요. 같은 뜻의 한자어 '육안'은 뉴스나 설명문에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means seeing with your eyes alone, without glasses, a telescope or a microscope. It mostly appears as '맨눈으로'. The Sino-Korean word '육안' has the same meaning and shows up more in news and explanatory writing.

examples.en: The kids are kicking a ball on the bare ground.
It rained, so the bare ground became muddy.
If you sit on the bare ground, your bottom gets cold.
The playground was bare ground with not a blade of grass.
This flower grows well even on bare ground.
It was hard to pitch a tent on the bare ground.

explain: 풀이나 바닥재 없이 흙이 그대로 드러난 땅이에요. 집 안 바닥에는 보통 '맨바닥'을 쓰고, '맨땅'은 밖의 흙땅에 써요. '맨-'은 아무것도 덮이거나 더해지지 않았다는 뜻으로 '맨손, 맨발'에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 아무 경험 없이 가게를 열어서 맨땅에 헤딩하는 기분이에요.
phrases.en: I opened a shop with no experience, so it feels like I'm starting from nothing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비나 도움 없이 처음부터 무작정 부딪쳐 보는 상황에 써요. 주로 말할 때 쓰는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you take on something from zero with no preparation or help. Mostly colloquial.
phrases.en_equiv: start from scratch; go in blind

explain_en: It is ground where the soil is exposed, with no grass or paving. For floors inside a building people usually say '맨바닥', while '맨땅' is for outdoor soil. The prefix '맨-' means nothing is covering or added, as in 맨손 and 맨발.

examples.ko: 맨몸으로 할 수 있는 운동을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me exercises I can do without equipment.

examples.ko: 그는 가방도 없이 맨몸으로 집을 나왔어요.
examples.en: He left the house empty-handed, without even a bag.

examples.ko: 맨몸 운동은 헬스장에 가지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: Bodyweight exercise doesn't require going to a gym.

examples.ko: 불이 나서 맨몸으로 겨우 도망쳐 나왔대요.
examples.en: I heard there was a fire and they barely escaped with nothing.

examples.ko: 맨몸으로 시작해서 지금은 가게가 두 개예요.
examples.en: I started with nothing, and now I have two shops.
Going out with nothing in hand, without a bag, feels light.

explain: 일상에서는 옷을 벗은 몸보다 도구나 재산 없이 몸 하나뿐인 상태를 말할 때 많이 써요. '맨몸 운동'은 기구 없이 자기 몸무게로 하는 운동이에요. 옷을 안 입은 몸은 보통 '알몸'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily speech it is used more for having only your own body, with no tools or money, than for being unclothed. '맨몸 운동' is exercise done with your own body weight and no equipment. For a body without clothes, people usually say '알몸'.

examples.en: It's cold to sit on the bare floor, so I put down a cushion.
The child is sleeping on the bare floor.

examples.ko: 침대 없이 맨바닥에서 잔 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once slept on the bare floor without a bed.
I spilled water on the bare floor and wiped it with a rag.
When I took up the carpet, the bare floor showed.
It's cold, so don't just lie down on the bare floor.

explain: 방석이나 돗자리, 카펫 같은 것을 아무것도 깔지 않은 바닥이에요. 집 안 바닥에도 쓰고 밖의 땅에도 쓸 수 있어요. 흙땅을 강조할 때는 '맨땅'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a floor or ground with nothing laid on it, such as a cushion, mat or carpet. It works for indoor floors as well as outdoor ground. To stress bare soil, people say '맨땅'.

examples.en: In winter it's too cold when your bare skin is exposed.
Mosquitoes pick only the bare skin to bite.

examples.ko: 맨살에 바로 닿는 옷은 부드러워야 해요.
examples.en: Clothes that touch your bare skin directly should be soft.
I spread sunscreen evenly on my bare skin.
The bare skin of my arm got red from the sun.

examples.ko: 맨살 위에 바로 입으면 따가운 옷이에요.
examples.en: This is a piece of clothing that itches if you wear it right on your skin.

explain: 옷이나 털에 덮이지 않고 그대로 드러난 살이에요. 그냥 '피부'는 일반적인 말이고, '맨살'은 가려지지 않은 상태를 강조해요. '맨살이 드러나다', '맨살에 닿다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is skin that is not covered by clothes or hair and is simply exposed. '피부' is the general word for skin, while '맨살' stresses that it is uncovered. It is often used as '맨살이 드러나다' or '맨살에 닿다'.

examples.en: I had no appetite, so I drank only plain water.

examples.ko: 이 국은 맛이 없고 꼭 맹물 같아요.
examples.en: This soup has no flavor, just like plain water.
Take the medicine with plain water.

examples.ko: 속이 안 좋아서 맹물로 입을 헹궜어요.
examples.en: My stomach felt bad, so I rinsed my mouth with plain water.

examples.ko: 라면을 끓일 때 맹물 대신 육수를 써 봤어요.
examples.en: When boiling ramyeon, I tried using broth instead of plain water.

examples.ko: 차를 마시지 않고 그냥 맹물을 마셔요.
examples.en: I don't drink tea, I just drink plain water.

explain: 차, 설탕, 맛 같은 것이 아무것도 섞이지 않은 물이에요. 그냥 '물'이라고 해도 되지만, 맛이 없다고 말할 때 '맹물 같다'처럼 많이 써요. 가게에서 사 마시는 물은 보통 '생수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is water with nothing mixed in, no tea, sugar or flavor. You can simply say '물', but '맹물' is handy when saying something tastes like nothing, as in '맹물 같다'. Bottled drinking water is usually called '생수'.

examples.en: I got appendicitis and had emergency surgery.

examples.ko: 오른쪽 아랫배가 아프면 맹장염일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your lower right abdomen hurts, it could be appendicitis.
My younger sibling was hospitalized with appendicitis.
Appendicitis needs to be treated quickly.

examples.ko: 친구가 맹장염 수술을 하고 일주일 쉬었어요.
examples.en: My friend had appendicitis surgery and rested for a week.
I thought it was appendicitis, but it was just enteritis.

explain: 병원에서는 '충수염'이라고도 하지만, 일상에서는 '맹장염'이라는 말이 더 익숙해요. '맹장염에 걸리다', '맹장 수술을 받다'처럼 말해요. 비슷하게 들리는 '장염'은 장 전체의 염증이라 다른 병이에요.
explain_en: Doctors also say '충수염', but in everyday speech '맹장염' sounds more familiar. People say '맹장염에 걸리다' or '맹장 수술을 받다'. The similar-sounding '장염' is inflammation of the intestines in general, which is a different condition.

examples.ko: 아버지는 머리숱이 많아서 머리 손질이 어려워요.
examples.en: My father has thick hair, so styling it is hard.
My hair has been thinning lately and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 머리숱이 적은 사람에게 어울리는 머리 모양이 있어요.
examples.en: There are hairstyles that suit people with thin hair.

examples.ko: 미용실에서 머리숱을 좀 쳐 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the hair salon to thin my hair a bit.
I have a lot of hair, so I get hot in summer.
Is there really a shampoo that makes your hair thicker?

explain: 머리카락의 굵기나 색이 아니라 양이 많고 적음을 말해요. '머리숱이 많다/적다'처럼 쓰고, 줄여서 그냥 '숱이 많다'라고도 해요. 미용실에서 머리카락을 얇게 덜어 낼 때는 '숱을 치다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is about how much hair you have, not how thick or what color it is. You say '머리숱이 많다/적다', or just '숱이 많다' for short. At a salon, thinning out the hair is called '숱을 치다'.

examples.en: Please squirt mustard on the hot dog.
Mustard sauce is a little spicy and tangy.
I spread a thin layer of mustard on the bread.

examples.ko: 케첩 말고 머스터드를 더 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me more mustard instead of ketchup?
If you don't have mustard, you can use mayonnaise.
Even a little mustard makes the taste strong.

explain: 서양식 노란 소스를 말하고, 핫도그나 샌드위치 같은 음식에 많이 써요. 한국어의 '겨자'도 mustard를 뜻하지만, 냉면이나 겨자채에 쓰는 매운 겨자를 떠올리는 경우가 많아요. 꿀을 섞은 '허니머스터드'도 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to the yellow Western-style sauce used on hot dogs and sandwiches. The Korean word '겨자' also means mustard, but it often brings to mind the hot mustard used with cold noodles or 겨자채. You will also often see 'honey mustard', called '허니머스터드'.

examples.ko: 비행기가 높이 올라가면 기압이 낮아져서 귀가 먹먹해져요.
examples.en: When a plane climbs high, the air pressure drops and my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 건물 안에서 누군가의 울음소리가 새어 나와서 가슴이 먹먹했어요.
examples.en: Someone's crying leaked out from inside the building and my chest felt heavy.
Maybe I have a cold, my ears feel stuffed.

examples.ko: 수영을 하고 나왔더니 귀가 먹먹한데 물이 들어갔나 봐요.
examples.en: My ears feel blocked after swimming. Maybe water got in.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보고 나니 가슴이 먹먹해서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: After the sad movie my chest felt so heavy that I couldn't speak.
When we entered the tunnel, my ears felt blocked.

explain: 귀에 쓰면 물이나 기압 때문에 소리가 잘 안 들리고 막힌 느낌이에요. 가슴에 쓰면 슬픔이나 감동이 가득 차서 말이 잘 안 나오는 느낌이에요. 귀가 막힌 느낌은 '멍멍하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: With ears, it means a blocked, muffled feeling where sounds are hard to hear because of water or pressure. With the chest, it means sadness or emotion fills you so much that words won't come. The blocked-ear feeling can also be called '멍멍하다'.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 먹보라서 간식이 금방 없어져요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a big eater, so the snacks disappear quickly.
Our dog is a total glutton.

examples.ko: 먹보인 친구랑 맛집에 가면 항상 즐거워요.
examples.en: It's always fun to go to a good restaurant with my foodie friend.
Don't tease me as a glutton just because I eat a lot.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 먹보여서 뷔페에 가면 접시를 몇 번이나 채워요.
examples.en: That friend is a big eater, so at a buffet they fill their plate many times.

examples.ko: 우리 아기는 먹보라서 분유를 금방 다 먹어요.
examples.en: Our baby is a big eater and finishes the formula quickly.

explain: 음식을 많이 먹는 사람이나 동물을 가볍고 친근하게 부르는 말이에요. 장난스럽게 쓰는 말이라서 어른에게 직접 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. '울보', '잠보'처럼 '-보'가 붙은 말이 더 있어요.
explain_en: It is a light, friendly name for a person or animal that eats a lot. Because it is playful, saying it directly to an adult can be rude. There are other '-보' words like '울보' (crybaby) and '잠보' (sleepyhead).

examples.en: After work, I had dinner in the food alley.

examples.ko: 이 동네 먹자골목에는 식당이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: The food alley in this neighborhood has a lot of restaurants.
The food alley is crowded on weekend evenings.
There's a famous tteokbokki place at the end of the food alley.
What shall we eat in the food alley next to the market?

examples.ko: 대학교 앞 먹자골목은 값이 싸서 학생들이 많이 가요.
examples.en: The food alley in front of the university is cheap, so many students go.

explain: 음식점과 술집이 줄지어 있는 골목을 말해요. 보통 동네나 대학교, 회사 근처에 있어서 '오늘 먹자골목 갈래요?'처럼 가볍게 말해요. 더 넓은 거리는 '맛집 거리'나 '음식점 거리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a lane lined with restaurants and eateries. It is usually near a neighborhood, university or office, and people casually say things like '오늘 먹자골목 갈래요?'. A broader street of restaurants is called a '맛집 거리' or '음식점 거리'.

examples.en: I dust off the bookshelf with a duster.
Do you happen to know where the duster is?
The new duster has soft fibers.
With just one duster, cleaning is easy.
I wiped with a dry towel instead of a duster.
Mom looked around the room holding a duster.

explain: 털이 달린 막대처럼 생긴 청소 도구로, 쌓인 먼지를 털어 낼 때 써요. 먼지는 '털다', 더러운 곳은 '닦다'로 구분해서 말해요. 걸레는 닦는 도구이고 먼지떨이는 터는 도구예요.
explain_en: It is a cleaning tool, like a stick with fibers, used to flick off built-up dust. Korean separates '털다' (shake or flick off dust) from '닦다' (wipe dirty spots). A rag is for wiping, while a '먼지떨이' is for flicking dust.

examples.en: The children just stood far off and watched.
I parked the car far away and walked.
I was scared of the dog, so I went around at a distance.

examples.ko: 멀찌감치 떨어져서 보면 그림이 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you stand far back, you can see the painting better.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 나를 보고 멀찌감치 피해 갔어요.
examples.en: That person saw me and steered clear at a distance.
Drive keeping a good distance from the car ahead.

explain: 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있는 모양을 나타내요. 그냥 '멀리'보다 일부러 거리를 두거나 떨어져 있는 상황에 잘 어울려요. '멀찍이'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It describes being quite far away. Compared with plain '멀리', it fits well when someone keeps their distance on purpose. '멀찍이' is used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 방문을 열려다가 안에서 소리가 나서 멈칫했어요.
examples.en: I was about to open the door, but I heard a sound inside and froze.

examples.ko: 이름을 부르자 그 사람이 멈칫하고 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, he paused for a moment and looked back.
A dog appeared and I hesitated without realizing.
I hesitated for a moment at the hard question.

examples.ko: 그가 말을 하다가 멈칫하더니 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He stopped short while talking and just smiled.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 모두 멈칫해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone froze at the news and couldn't say a word.

explain: 놀라거나 망설여서 하던 동작을 순간적으로 멈출 때 써요. '멈추다'는 완전히 서는 것이고, '멈칫하다'는 아주 잠깐 멈추는 느낌이에요. '멈칫 서다'처럼 '멈칫'만 부사로 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Used when you stop what you're doing for an instant out of surprise or hesitation. '멈추다' means stopping fully, while '멈칫하다' is a very brief pause. The root '멈칫' can also be used alone as an adverb, as in '멈칫 서다'.

examples.ko: 나는 정말 멍텅구리처럼 길을 잘못 들었어요.
examples.en: I took the wrong road like a total fool.

examples.ko: 멍텅구리 같은 실수를 또 해서 속상해요.
examples.en: I'm upset because I made a silly mistake again.
The younger sibling teased the older brother, calling him a fool.

examples.ko: 이렇게 쉬운 걸 몰랐다니, 내가 멍텅구리였어요.
examples.en: I didn't know something this easy. I was such a fool.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 멍텅구리가 아니라 생각보다 영리해요.
examples.en: That person isn't a fool but is smarter than you'd think.

examples.ko: 멍텅구리처럼 서 있지 말고 좀 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there like a dummy, help me out.

explain: 어리석거나 둔한 사람을 놀리듯이 부르는 말이에요. 가족이나 친구끼리 장난으로 쓰고, 처음 만난 사람이나 어른에게 쓰면 모욕이 돼요. '바보'보다 조금 장난스럽게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a teasing name for someone foolish or slow. Family and friends use it jokingly, but to a stranger or an elder it is insulting. It can sound a bit more playful than '바보'.

examples.en: I feel sick because of motion sickness.

examples.ko: 빈속에 약을 먹으면 속이 메스꺼울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Taking medicine on an empty stomach can make you nauseous.
When I see blood I feel sick, so I close my eyes.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 음식이 안 맞았는지 속이 메스꺼웠어요.
examples.en: Maybe the food I ate yesterday didn't agree with me, I felt nauseous.

examples.ko: 속이 메스껍고 어지러워서 일찍 집에 갔어요.
examples.en: I felt sick and dizzy, so I went home early.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 거짓말은 듣기만 해도 메스꺼워요.
examples.en: That person's lies make me sick just to hear.

explain: 토할 것 같은 속의 느낌이에요. 'ㅂ 불규칙'이라서 '메스꺼워요, 메스꺼운'으로 바뀌고 '매스껍다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 자꾸 속이 불편할 때는 '메슥거리다', 배가 흔들리듯 불편할 때는 '울렁거리다'가 잘 맞아요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of being about to throw up. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective (메스꺼워요, 메스꺼운), and '매스껍다' is used with the same meaning. '메슥거리다' fits a repeatedly upset stomach, and '울렁거리다' fits a queasy, rolling feeling.

en: feel sick; feel like throwing up

examples.ko: 아침마다 속이 메슥거려서 밥을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: My stomach feels sick every morning, so I can't eat.

examples.ko: 차 안에서 책을 읽으면 속이 메슥거려요.
examples.en: If I read a book in the car, my stomach turns.
The smell was so strong that I began to feel sick.
My stomach feels sick, so I can't eat anything.

examples.ko: 약을 먹은 뒤에 속이 좀 메슥거렸어요.
examples.en: After taking the medicine, my stomach felt a bit queasy.

examples.ko: 속이 계속 메슥거리면 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If your stomach keeps feeling sick, go see a doctor.

explain: 토할 것 같아서 속이 자꾸 불편한 느낌을 말해요. 주로 '속이 메슥거리다'라고 해요. '메스껍다'는 그 상태를 말하고, '메슥거리다'는 계속 반복되는 느낌이 더 강해요. 파도처럼 속이 흔들리는 느낌은 '울렁거리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes an upset stomach that keeps feeling like you might throw up, usually as '속이 메슥거리다'. '메스껍다' names the state, while '메슥거리다' stresses that the feeling keeps recurring. A stomach rolling like waves is '울렁거리다'.

examples.en: If you shout in the mountains, it echoes.
In an empty gym even small sounds echo.
His words are still echoing in my ears.
The sound of the bell echoed long through the valley.
The singing echoed loudly inside the tunnel.

examples.ko: 친구 이름을 부르자 목소리가 메아리쳐 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: When I called my friend's name, my voice came back as an echo.

explain: 소리가 부딪혀서 되돌아와 울리는 것을 말해요. 산에서 '야호!' 하고 외치면 돌아오는 소리가 '메아리'예요. 잊히지 않고 마음에 계속 남는 말을 '귓가에 메아리치다'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It means a sound bounces back and rings out again. The sound that returns when you shout '야호!' in the mountains is a '메아리'. It is also used figuratively, as in '귓가에 메아리치다', for words that stay with you.

examples.en: The child is wearing overalls.
The strap keeps slipping down, which is uncomfortable.
The bag strap presses on my shoulder and it hurts.
Grandfather wears suspenders on his trousers.
Could you shorten the strap length a bit?
I hear skirts with straps are in fashion these days.

explain: 바지를 어깨에 걸어 고정하는 끈이에요. 가방을 어깨에 메는 끈도 '멜빵'이라고 해요. 멜빵이 달린 바지는 붙여서 '멜빵바지'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the strap that holds trousers up over the shoulders. The strap you carry a bag on is also called '멜빵'. Pants with such straps are written together as '멜빵바지'.

examples.en: The razor blade is dull, so my face stings.

examples.ko: 면도날은 한 달에 한 번 바꿔요.
examples.en: I replace the razor blade once a month.
Be careful not to cut yourself on the razor blade.
I went to the mart to buy a new razor blade.

examples.ko: 면도날과 칫솔 같은 소모품은 정기 배송으로 받고 있어요.
examples.en: I get supplies like razor blades and toothbrushes through regular delivery.
If the razor blade rusts, don't use it, throw it away.

explain: 면도기에 끼워서 수염이나 털을 깎는 날이에요. 날이 잘 안 들 때는 '무디다'라고 하고, 새것으로 '갈아 끼우다'라고 말해요. 요즘은 일회용 면도기나 교체형 면도날을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the blade fitted in a razor to shave facial or body hair. A blade that doesn't cut well is called '무디다', and you '갈아 끼우다' to swap in a new one. These days many people use disposable razors or replaceable blades.
